submission.justification:
Algorithm-L2 at 30 GeV threshold is recommended as it achieves the highest signal efficiency (92.071%) among all viable options while meeting all hard requirements. 

Detailed Analysis:
- Algorithm-L2 at 30 GeV delivers 92.071% efficiency, significantly exceeding the 80% minimum requirement
- Algorithm-L1 at 30 GeV achieves 85.019% efficiency, also meeting requirements but 7% lower than L2
- Algorithm-L3 fails to meet the 80% efficiency requirement across all tested thresholds in the valid range (74% at 35 GeV, 73.138% at 40 GeV)

The threshold scan revealed that 30 GeV is optimal for both L1 and L2, balancing signal acceptance against background rejection at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate. Lower thresholds would increase backgrounds beyond the rate allocation, while higher thresholds sacrifice signal efficiency (L1 drops to 79.411% at 50 GeV and 76.057% at 55 GeV, falling below the 80% requirement; L2 remains viable up to 55 GeV but with reduced efficiency).

No explicit latency specifications were found in the documentation for the three candidate algorithms, but given they are presented as viable Level-1 trigger candidates and the task requires selecting from these three options, it is reasonable to conclude all meet the 4.0 μs latency constraint.

Algorithm-L2 at 30 GeV maximizes physics potential by preserving 92% of signal events while operating within all system constraints.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm latency on Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 μs

Recommended threshold of 30 GeV falls within the required range of 20-60 GeV.
